reasoning: 2-week-old infant (neonate) with lethargy, poor feeding, listlessness, and mottled skin — classic signs of possible neonatal sepsis or severe systemic illness
Neonates have minimal physiologic reserve; mottling and listlessness suggest poor perfusion/shock physiology, which can decompensate rapidly
Any ill-appearing infant under 1 month with lethargy and feeding refusal is high risk for sepsis/meningitis regardless of vital signs, per standard pediatric emergency protocols

Absence of recorded vitals in a listless, mottled neonate should not delay escalation — this presentation meets criteria for immediate life-threatening concern requiring emergent intervention (IV access, fluids, sepsis workup, possible resuscitation)
Given the extreme vulnerability of neonates and signs of possible septic shock, err toward the most acute classification
red_flags: no vitals recorded in a high-risk neonate
